issues.description: Constructor 'Bitmap24' signature mismatch: the template header declares Bitmap24(long i_width, long i_height) while the template implementation defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height). The solution header uses Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height). This inconsistency between the declaration (template header) and definition (template .cpp) will cause a compilation/linkage error for students using the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor declaration and definition consistent. Update example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp in the template to declare 'Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height);' to match the implementation in Bitmap24.cpp (or alternatively change the implementation to use 'long' if that is the intended type). The recommended fix is to change the header to use 'int' so it matches the .cpp and the solution.

issues.description: Constructor for the Bitmap24 class has inconsistent parameter types between the template header and the implementation. Template header declares: 'Bitmap24(long i_width, long i_height);' (TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY: example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) while the template implementation defines: 'Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height)' (TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY: example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp). The solution repository consistently uses 'int' for the constructor in both header and implementation. This mismatch of parameter types (long vs int) means the out-of-class definition does not match the declared signature in the class, which can cause compilation errors and prevents students from reliably mapping the class API (header) to its implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent in the template to match the implementation and the solution. Change the declaration in TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'Bitmap24(long i_width, long i_height);' to 'Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height);' (or alternatively, change the implementation to use 'long' in both declaration and definition). Prefer aligning the template with the solution by using 'int' to avoid compilation/signature mismatches and reduce student confusion.
